title: Large language models accurately predict public perceptions of support for climate action worldwide

bias_targets.methodology: Regressing LLM prediction errors (Mean Absolute Error) against macro-structural country features, specifically GDP per capita and internet penetration, to demonstrate that models perform worse in poorer and less digitally connected settings due to representation bias in training data.

Comparing prediction accuracy of public opinion perception gaps across 125 different countries and conducting counterfactual perturbation tests that swap country names (e.g., assigning a poor country's name to a rich country's covariates) to test if models rely on memorized national associations rather than structural reasoning.
